items: GC sirf volatile (aasani se bhaap banne wali) cheezon ke liye kaam karti hai.
Samples thermally stable (garmi mein na tootne wale) hone chahiye. Jo compounds zyada temperature par toot jate hain, un par GC istemal nahi ho sakti.
Proteins aur polymers jaise bare biomolecules GC se nahi jaanche ja sakte kyunke yeh aasani se bhaap nahi bante.
GC ke instruments (aalaat) aur un ki maintenance (dekh bhaal) ka kharcha zyada hai.

blocks.title: GC mass spectrometry ke saath
blocks.text: Forensic kaam mein GC aksar mass spectrometer ke saath jori jati hai (GC-MS). Column se nikalne wala har component seedha mass spectrometer mein jata hai; us ka spectrum batata hai ke yeh kaun si cheez hai, aur peak ka area batata hai ke kitni hai, chahe miqdar bohat thori ho.

Lactic acid, CH₃CH(OH)COOH, ke aik impure (na-khalis) sample mein sirf butanone ki contamination (milawat) hai. Is mixture ko gas chromatography se jaancha jata hai. Butanone ka retention time lactic acid se zyada (longer) paaya jata hai.

blocks.prompt: (i) Mobile aur stationary phase ke liye suitable (munasib) cheezein batayein.
blocks.explanation: Mobile phase: koi inert carrier gas, jaise helium ya nitrogen. Stationary phase: silica ya alumina ke particles par laga hua non-volatile, ooncha boiling point wala liquid (jaise lambi chain wala hydrocarbon).

blocks.prompt: (ii) Gas chromatogram se mixture ki percentage composition kaise maloom karenge?
blocks.explanation: Pehle retention time se peaks pehchanein. Har peak ka area napein (½ × base × height). Butanone ki % = butanone peak ka area ÷ (dono peaks ke areas ka jor) × 100; isi tarah lactic acid ki %.

items: GC: mobile phase = inert carrier gas (He, N₂); stationary phase = silica ya alumina par non-volatile liquid.
Retention time se component ki pehchan; peak ka area (½ × base × height) se us ki miqdar.
% of A = A ka peak area ÷ sab peaks ke areas ka jor × 100.
Sirf volatile aur garmi mein stable samples; forensics, industry, khurak aur medicine mein istemal.
